value.ruling: addressable but unreachable... outside of bugs, or things we haven't built yet... every device, including the bus itself and the ground loop, has a presence on the bus and can respond to a health query... so the basics of this has to be in the base shim. As to census... what census?
value.successor: the presence protocol (every device answers a standard verb set, reachable identically from CLI, bus and web) — its own /intent, this ticket's parent once cast
value.what_it_also_killed: This ticket's own assumption-kill. It had ruled that 'a device nobody addresses needs no receive, so red means ADDRESSED-BUT-UNREACHABLE, never lacks-receive'. Akien's spec is stronger and simpler: EVERY device — the bus and the ground loop included — is addressable and answers. There is no legitimate non-answerer, so unreachable is red universally, and the two exceptions he names (bugs, things not yet built) are exactly the things that SHOULD be red. Law 9 falls out rather than being applied by hand.
value.what_it_killed: THE CENSUS, entirely. This ticket proposed measuring code structure — does a device's class declare receive, which channels does it accept — as the way to find unreachable devices. If every device answers a health query, that is a PROXY read instead of the thing: you ask the running device rather than reading its class. cairn/tools/orient's own charter names that exact failure as its founding why ('a proxy was read instead of the thing'), and the census was proposed inside orient. Withdrawn, not defended.
value.what_survives: The aim, and every repair child. Mail arriving is one case of a device being reachable; the tracking half moves to the successor node, where the health sweep — ask every device on the roster, no answer is red — does what the census was invented to do, with no code measurement at all.

value.and: MURDERBOT — 'so that's how bounce messages would be visible. something visible in that public feed and maybe with it's bounce message.'
value.how_it_travels: On `announce`, the sender's PUBLIC feed, with the envelope's existing reply_to naming the dead message. No fifth channel: announce is a RECORD channel, so a delivery failure never collapses and never expires (Law 7), and the bounce is visible to anyone reading the feed rather than only to whoever reads the drain's return value. It also terminates for free — a bounce is a FEED POST, not a DELIVERY, so there is nothing there to bounce, and no hop counter is needed.
value.note_on_a_sibling: This ticket's child the-librarian-accepts-personal had already measured the invented 'chat' channel at cairn/devices/librarian/trees.py. Akien's Murderbot ruling confirms it and widens it: 'chat' is not a channel at all — the chat PANE is the view over announce + personal, exactly as the console pane is the view over info + debug. The same invention also sits at cairn/devices/web_server/render.py:165, which that child did not reach. Both addresses are retired by every-device-has-a-presence :: the-pane-set-is-the-channel-set.
value.ruling: every device can send and recieve messages over the bus via the shims. whether the device can do anything with the message is a contract between the shim and the device... what happens when the shim recieves a message that there is no handler for. is it dropped? return to sender? trouble ticket? trouble ticket from the device that receieved the return to sender? that might be best actually. then it's just renegotiate the contract.
value.what_it_moved: The RAISE, off the bus and onto the SENDER. This ticket's child undeliverable-mail-raises-its-own-trouble had the bus raising a trouble for mail it could not hand over. Akien's mechanism routes the failure to the party whose assumption is broken instead: the message goes back, and the device that receives the return raises the trouble. The disposition comes with it — 'renegotiate the contract' — so the trouble has a fix rather than being a marker.
value.what_survives_here: The measurement (the live drain, the classification, the dedup) and every other repair child. Only the raise moved.

value: RESOLVED BY THE AMENDMENT — 'what event fires the census' is moot; there is no census. The live form of the question moves to the successor node: at what CADENCE is the health query asked. It is real there, because asking everyone every beat is a poll, and yet asking IS the measurement (you cannot learn a device is alive by waiting for it to fail). A /chart decompose question, not a guess.

MAY A MEASUREMENT AUTO-CLEAR A TROUBLE? Survives the amendment unchanged. The trouble lane's clear is per-recipient and demands what_changed, and was designed around a human witness naming the fix. A measurement in that slot is arguably stronger evidence, but it changes what prior_attempts counts — flaps rather than failed fixes. Left open deliberately; it is a /chart question.
